newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia approves oil/mineral reserves list.
newsitem.headline: Russia approves oil/mineral reserves list.

text.p: Russia's upper parliament house gave final approval on Thursday to a list of seven energy and mineral deposits open to development under production-sharing deals.

The approval means BHP Petroleum, a unit of Australian group The Broken Hill Proprietary Company Ltd, may be able to proceed with its proposal to tap the Barents Sea's Prirazlomnoye oilfield, which was on the list.
It also means Canadian mining concern Echo Bay Mines Ltd may forge ahead to tap the Kuranakh gold field in Siberia's Sakha republic.
Deputies approved the list with 127 votes in favour of the bill, eleven against and 10 abstentions. The bill must now be approved by President Boris Yeltsin.

Parliament expects investment in the seven fields to total $16.5 billion, including $1 billion in foreign investment. But Russian companies do not have the resources needed for the fields in which foreign investors will not participate.

The other five approved deposits, open only to domestic investors, are the giant Samotlor oil and gas condensate field, the Krasnoleninskoye oil deposit, the Yakovlevskoye iron ore deposit, the Romanshkinskoye oil field and oil deposits near Russia's Far Eastern island of Sakhalin.

The upper house's approval is a tiny victory for foreign energy investors overall, who want a comprehensive list of the reserves open to investment enshrined in law rather than a piece-meal approach parcelling out deposits over time.
Parliament will consider a second list of nine reserves open to production-sharing when it reconvenes in autumn.

Russia has a production-sharing law, but most U.S., Japanese, European and other oil companies must have their projects approved before proceeding with tens of billions of dollars in planned investments.
